The type of tibial component used in unicompartmental knee replacement (UKR) can impact mechanical alignment. Patients who received a metal-backed Onlay tibial component obtained better postoperative mechanical alignment compared to those who received all-polyethylene Inlay prostheses.

The thicker overall construct of the Onlay prosthesis appears to be an important determinant of postoperative alignment, suggesting that it may provide improved stability and support for the knee joint. Additionally, studies have shown that Onlay components are associated with higher survivorship rates and improved postoperative mechanical alignment compared to Inlay components.

However, other factors can also influence mechanical alignment, such as the level of arthritis, age, gender, visibility of landmarks, and misalignment. A new assessment method has been suggested to assess joint line positions by means of radiographs of the contralateral knee, which may provide a more accurate measurement of mechanical alignment.

Therefore, while Onlay components are generally associated with better mechanical alignment in UKR, other factors must be considered when making treatment decisions, and a thorough evaluation of individual patient characteristics is necessary to determine the best course of treatment.
